“Certainty is not attained by imitation, but by tasting (direct experience).” — Al-Ghazali (Deliverance from Error (related))

Source context

Archive record: this English passage is associated with Deliverance from Error (related), within the Islamic Philosophy tradition. Use the cited work or edition when a scholarly attribution is needed.

A short reading

Read in the register of certainty, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Al-Ghazali's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
